{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01AcNRnYANdtvmjfpN1Ayhsh","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# MedConnect, Inc. — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-16\n     4→Developer website: http://medconnecthealth.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→MedConnect, Inc. is a small, privately held health IT company headquartered in Montgomery, Alabama. Founded in 2004 by Jimmy Chapman, the company builds and sells MedConnectHealth, a cloud-based integrated EHR and practice management platform aimed at ambulatory physician practices. The company has approximately 11–50 employees (per LinkedIn) and operates out of a single office in Montgomery. MedConnect positions itself as an affordable, physician-designed alternative to larger EHR vendors, with pricing at $349/month per provider.\n     9→\n    10→MedConnect has a close relationship with MediSYS, Inc. (medisysinc.com), which appears to serve as a distribution/support partner — MediSYS's website describes providing \"local, expert support, customizations, onsite implementation and continued training since 2006\" for MedConnect EHR. Earlier versions of the product (e.g., MedConnect v2.3) appear on MediSYS press releases, suggesting that MediSYS may have originally developed or co-developed the platform, while MedConnect, Inc. is the certified developer entity. The exact corporate relationship is not fully clear from public sources.\n    11→\n    12→The company claims to support over 25 medical specialties with connectivity to over 30 hospitals and labs/diagnostics. Its customer base appears concentrated in Alabama, with notable integrations specific to that state (direct connection to Blue Cross/Blue Shield of Alabama, connection to Alabama's One Health Record HIE). MedConnect was recognized as the first ambulatory EHR vendor to connect to Alabama's One Health Record HIE network. The product is not listed on major review platforms like G2 or Capterra, suggesting a small customer base and limited national presence.\n    13→\n    14→Patient data is hosted at a Tier-4 data center. The product is entirely cloud-based and browser-accessible, requiring no on-premise hardware or software installation.\n    15→\n    16→## Product: MedConnectHealth\n    17→\n    18→CHPL IDs: 9183\n    19→\n    20→### What It Is\n    21→\n    22→MedConnectHealth 3.0 is a cloud-based, integrated healthcare software platform combining EHR, practice management, scheduling, patient portal, patient kiosk, and telehealth into a single product. It is ONC 2015 Edition certified (certified December 12, 2017) across a broad set of criteria spanning clinical documentation, e-prescribing, transitions of care, patient access, clinical quality measures, public health reporting, and FHIR APIs. The certified product number is 15.04.04.1889.MedC.03.00.1.171212.\n    23→\n    24→The SED intended user description is \"Outpatient Clinic,\" indicating it is designed for ambulatory care settings. The product appears to be the vendor's single, integrated offering — there are no separately named or marketed sub-products beyond the modules described below.\n    25→\n    26→### Users & Market\n    27→\n    28→**Target users:** Physicians, clinical staff, billing staff, and practice managers in ambulatory/outpatient settings. Patients interact through the patient portal and kiosk.\n    29→\n    30→**Clinical settings:** Ambulatory clinics and physician group practices. The product supports over 25 specialties (specific specialties not enumerated on the vendor's website). The product appears oriented toward small to mid-size physician practices rather than hospitals or health systems.\n    31→\n    32→**Geographic focus:** Strong Alabama presence, with direct integrations to Blue Cross/Blue Shield of Alabama and the Alabama One Health Record HIE. The extent of out-of-state deployment is unclear.\n    33→\n    34→**Customer scale:** Not disclosed. The small company size (~11–50 employees), absence from major review platforms, and regional focus suggest a relatively small customer base, likely in the hundreds of practices or fewer.\n    35→\n    36→**No notable named customers** are publicly identified on the vendor's website. Bingham Healthcare (in Idaho) appears in search results as having a \"MedConnect\" patient portal, though this may be a different \"MedConnect\" product unrelated to this vendor.\n    37→\n    38→### Modules & Functionality\n    39→\n    40→Based on vendor website product pages, the platform includes the following integrated modules:\n    41→\n    42→**EHR / Clinical Documentation:**\n    43→- \"One-Click\" options for patient history, review of systems, and physical exam documentation\n    44→- Multiple documentation methods: voice recognition, point-and-click, document scanning, image annotation\n    45→- Configurable templates by provider specialty\n    46→- Patient chart displaying medications, lab results, problem lists, allergies, vitals, flowsheets, immunizations, and scanned documents\n    47→- Financial information visible within the patient chart\n    48→- Care plan management with diagnosis documentation accessible to patients\n    49→- Patient education resources customizable by clinic, routed to patient portal\n    50→- AI-described as \"advanced clinical support tools\" (details sparse)\n    51→\n    52→**E-Prescribing:**\n    53→- Surescripts Certified for electronic prescribing including controlled substances (EPCS)\n    54→- Contraindication checking and formulary status verification\n    55→- Partnership with DrFirst for e-prescribing functionality\n    56→\n    57→**Orders & Results / Lab Integration:**\n    58→- Integrated orders with patient flow\n    59→- Automatic lab test triggers based on exam findings\n    60→- Interfaces with LabCorp, Quest Diagnostics, and other lab companies\n    61→- Lab results populate directly into patient notes\n    62→- Connectivity to over 30 hospitals and labs/diagnostics\n    63→\n    64→**Practice Management / Billing:**\n    65→- Claims management with charges categorized by Pending Processing, Submission, and Rework\n    66→- Electronic and paper claim generation\n    67→- Claims transmission via multiple clearinghouses: ClaimMD, Change Healthcare, Trizetto, Navicure, Waystar\n    68→- Direct connection to Blue Cross/Blue Shield of Alabama\n    69→- Automatic downloading of electronic immunizations, vitals, lab results (discrete and from interfaced labs), clinical notes/documentation (structured and free-text), review of systems, physical exam findings, care plans, patient education materials delivered, scanned documents and images.\n   133→\n   134→**Orders and results:** Lab orders, diagnostic orders, order results populated from external labs (LabCorp, Quest, etc.).\n   135→\n   136→**Prescriptions:** E-prescribing data including controlled substances, formulary checks, contraindication alerts, prescription history (via Surescripts/DrFirst integration).\n   137→\n   138→**Scheduling data:** Appointments, provider schedules, templates, appointment types, reminder communications.\n   139→\n   140→**Financial/billing data:** Charges, claims (electronic and paper), remittance advice (ERAs), payment postings, patient balances, copay collections, insurance eligibility responses, financial statements, collection letters, revenue reports. Direct claims data flows to BCBS Alabama and multiple clearinghouses.\n   141→\n   142→**Patient portal data:** Patient-submitted messages, medication refill requests, appointment requests, electronic form submissions (registration, consent, wellness), patient-downloaded records, bill pay transactions.\n   143→\n   144→**Kiosk/check-in data:** Scanned driver's licenses, scanned insurance cards, check-in timestamps, copay collection records, demographic updates.\n   145→\n   146→**Telehealth data:** Video visit session records (unclear how much session metadata vs. clinical documentation is retained).\n   147→\n   148→**Quality/reporting data:** Clinical quality measure calculations, PI reporting data, population health analytics.\n   149→\n   150→**Interoperability data:** C-CDA documents (sent/received), DIRECT messages, HIE exchange records, immunization registry submissions, syndromic surveillance submissions, cancer registry submissions.\n   151→\n   152→**Gaps/uncertainties:**\n   153→- The website does not describe document management or medical record scanning in detail beyond mentioning \"document scanning\" and \"scanned documents\" in the {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01CRB5Va8gnTapKSVTJY8t6w","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Gmw5HvK125j8RV1NxqaFvd","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/medconnect-inc--medconnecthealth/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# MedConnect, Inc. — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-16\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://medconnecthealth.com/electronic-health-information-export/\n- CHPL IDs: 9183\n- Product: MedConnectHealth 3.0\n- Certification date: 2017-12-12\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. Probed the registered URL with curl:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sI -L \"https://medconnecthealth.com/electronic-health-information-export/\" \\\n     -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36'\n   ```\n   Returned HTTP 200, Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8. WordPress site (Link headers point to wp-json endpoints). Curious custom headers: `Server: Commodore64`, `X-Powered-By: Sunshine and Rainbows`.\n\n2. Downloaded the full page HTML (49,778 bytes):\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://medconnecthealth.com/electronic-health-information-export/\" \\\n     -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o ehi-export-page.html\n   ```\n\n3. Searched page source for downloadable file links:\n   ```bash\n   grep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|xls|csv|json|doc|docx|yaml|yml)[^\"]*\"' ehi-export-page.html\n   ```\n   Found three PDFs:\n   - `EHI_Export_Documentation.pdf` — the EHI export documentation (relevant)\n   - `RealWorldTestResults2022.pdf` — real-world testing results (not relevant)\n   - `Xerox-Scan_10312022091038-rwt-updated.pdf` — scanned real-world testing doc (not relevant)\n\n4. Downloaded the EHI Export Documentation PDF:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://staging.medconnecthealth.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/EHI_Export_Documentation.pdf\" \\\n     -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o EHI_Export_Documentation.pdf\n   ```\n   Verified: `file EHI_Export_Documentation.pdf` → \"PDF document, version 1.6 (zip deflate encoded)\". 334,660 bytes, 1 page.\n\n5. Confirmed page content via WordPress REST API:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://www.medconnecthealth.com/wp-json/wp/v2/pages/2479\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n   ```\n   Page content is simply a single link to the PDF. Page published and last modified 2023-11-09.\n\n6. Navigated to the page in a browser. Screenshot confirms: the page has a heading \"Electronic Health Information Export\" and a single link labeled \"170.315(b)(10) EHI Export Documentation\" pointing to the PDF. No other substantive content — just the site footer and sidebar with recent blog posts.\n\n7. Checked the mandatory disclosures page (https://www.medconnecthealth.com/pricing/) for additional EHI documentation — found only a mention of \"170.315 (b)(10): Electronic Health Information Export\" in the certified criteria list, no additional links or content.\n\n8. Checked for embedded URLs, attachments within the PDF:\n   ```bash\n   pdfdetach -list EHI_Export_Documentation.pdf  # 0 embedded files\n   pdftotext EHI_Export_Documentation.pdf - | grep -oiE 'https?://[^ ]+'  # only self-referential URL\n   ```\n   The PDF contains only a self-referential link back to the same page (https://www.medconnecthealth.com/electronic-health-information-export/).\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a single 1-page PDF authored by Brett Chapman (created 2023-11-09 using Acrobat PDFMaker 23 for Word). The document contains:\n\n### Compliance Statement\nThe document restates the regulatory requirements of 170.315(b)(10), confirming that MedConnectHealth supports:\n- **Single patient EHI export**: Users can create export files for individual patients at any time, without developer assistance. Export capability is restricted to specific users or system administrators.\n- **Patient population EHI export**: Two options — individual exports for each patient, or a bulk export of all patients \"upon request\" (performed by MedConnectHealth, not self-service by the user).\n- **Documentation**: Links back to the registered URL.\n\n### Export Format\nThe export is a ZIP file containing a folder per patient/clinic with:\n- **C-CDA in compliance with USCDI v1** (XML format)\n- **Demographics** (PDF)\n- **Scanned Documents** (PDF, JPG, PNG)\n- **Clinical Notes/Lab Results** (PDF)\n\nThat is the complete description of the export format. There is no data dictionary, no field-level documentation, no schema files, no sample exports, and no API documentation.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nBased on the product research, MedConnectHealth stores data across many domains. The export format description reveals significant gaps:\n\n**Covered (at least partially):**\n- **Demographics** — exported as PDF (not computable)\n- **Clinical documentation** — C-CDA covers problems, medications, allergies, immunizations, vitals, lab results, procedures per USCDI v1\n- **Clinical notes** — exported as PDF\n- **Lab results** — exported as PDF\n- **Scanned documents** — exported as original formats (PDF, JPG, PNG)\n\n**Clearly missing or not mentioned:**\n- **Billing/financial data** — charges, claims, remittance advice, payment postings, patient balances, insurance eligibility. This is a major gap; MedConnectHealth has a full practice management/billing module.\n- **Prescriptions/e-prescribing history** — medication orders, EPCS data, formulary checks (beyond what's in the C-CDA medication list)\n- **Orders** — lab/diagnostic orders and their status\n- **Care plans and goals** — beyond what the C-CDA may contain\n- **Patient portal data** — messages, refill requests, appointment requests, electronic form submissions, bill pay history\n- **Kiosk/check-in data** — scanned IDs, insurance cards, check-in records\n- **Telehealth session data** — visit records, session metadata\n- **Quality/CQM data** — clinical quality measure calculations\n- **Interoperability records** — C-CDA documents sent/received, DIRECT messages, HIE exchange records\n- **Insurance/enrollment information** — beyond basic demographics\n\n**Ambiguous:**\n- The C-CDA \"in compliance with USCDI v1\" covers a defined subset of clinical data (problems, medications, allergies, immunizations, vitals, labs, procedures, health concerns, goals, assessments, care teams, clinical notes). However, C-CDA is a clinical summary standard — it does not naturally accommodate billing records, custom form data, or specialty-specific clinical data beyond what USCDI v1 defines.\n- \"Demographics (PDF)\" — exporting demographics as PDF rather than structured data means the information is not computably accessible. It's unclear if this PDF contains more demographic detail than the C-CDA header.\n- \"Clinical Notes/Lab Results (PDF)\" — unclear if these duplicate the C-CDA content or include additional notes/results not in the C-CDA.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses a hybrid approach:\n- **C-CDA XML** for structured clinical data (USCDI v1 scope)\n- **PDF** for demographics, clinical notes, and lab results\n- **Original format files** (PDF/JPG/PNG) for scanned documents\n- **ZIP packaging** with folder-per-patient structure\n\nThis is essentially a **USCDI v1 clinical summary plus scanned documents**, not a comprehensive EHI export. The C-CDA covers the (g)(10) clinical data slice, while the PDFs and scanned documents add some additional material — but the export entirely omits the practice management, billing, and specialty-specific data domains that constitute a large portion of the designated record set.\n\nThe heavy use of PDF is problematic: demographics and lab results in PDF are not computable. A third party could not import this data into another system without manual data entry or OCR for anything beyond the C-CDA XML content.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is extremely minimal:\n- **No data dictionary** — no field-level documentation of any kind\n- **No schema files** — no XSD, no C-CDA template constraints, no custom profile documentation\n- **No sample exports** — no example files showing what the export looks like\n- **No export instructions** — no screenshots or step-by-step guide for users\n- **No value set documentation** — no description of coded fields or terminology\n- **No format specification** beyond the 4-bullet folder structure\n\nThe document reads as a compliance checkbox — it restates the regulatory requirements verbatim and adds a minimal export format description. A developer could not implement an import of this data based solely on this documentation; they would need to know C-CDA independently and would have no guidance on the PDF content structure.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nThe documentation is a single page with two sections: a restatement of regulatory requirements and a 4-line export format description. There is:\n- No versioning or change history (though the PDF creation date is visible)\n- No entity/relationship documentation\n- No cardinality or constraint information\n- No description of how the population export differs structurally from the single-patient export\n- No documentation of the \"upon request\" bulk export process\n\n### (b)(10) vs (g)(10) Assessment\n\nThis export conflates (b)(10) and (g)(10). The C-CDA with USCDI v1 compliance is essentially the same clinical data scope as a (g)(10) patient summary. The addition of PDF demographics, scanned documents, and PDF clinical notes goes slightly beyond a pure C-CDA clinical summary, but the export still does not address the fundamental (b)(10) requirement: export of **all** electronic health information the product stores.\n\nMedConnectHealth is an integrated EHR + practice management platform with billing, scheduling, patient portal, kiosk, telehealth, and quality reporting modules. The export documentation describes a clinical summary plus document attachments — a small fraction of the total data the product manages about patients.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://medconnecthealth.com/electronic-health-information-export/ (no redirect)\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (PDF direct link works with curl)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link (one click from page to PDF)\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- No obstacles encountered. The URL was live, the PDF downloaded cleanly.\n- The page references `staging.medconnecthealth.com` in several internal links (including the PDF link), suggesting the site may have been migrated from a staging environment without updating internal URLs. Both staging and www domains resolve to the same content.\n- The PDF contains no embedded URLs or attachments pointing to additional documentation.\n- No additional EHI export documentation was found elsewhere on the site.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":808,"cache_read_input_tokens":56249,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":808},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"00052a02-36e6-4e11-90d8-9e85d631cc25","uuid":"2a9ac521-15bd-41a8-9e64-5b1dbe98a33f"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01Ar9rMpCEbak7ByjcWYzQUK","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done. Here's a summary of what was found:\n\n**MedConnect, Inc. — MedConnectHealth** has a single 1-page PDF as their entire EHI export documentation. The export is a ZIP file with per-patient folders containing:\n\n- C-CDA XML (USCDI v1) for structured clinical data\n- Demographics as PDF\n- Scanned documents (PDF/JPG/PNG)\n- Clinical notes/lab results as PDF\n\n**Key findings:**\n- **Extremely minimal documentation** — no data dictionary, no schema, no sample exports, no user guide\n- **Major coverage gaps** — billing, e-prescribing, orders, patient portal data, kiosk data, telehealth, and quality reporting data are all absent from the export\n- **Conflates (b)(10) with (g)(10)** — the C-CDA USCDI v1 export covers the same clinical summary scope as (g)(10), not the full designated record set\n- **Heavy PDF use** — demographics and lab results exported as non-computable PDFs\n- **Population export requires vendor assistance** — users can self-service single-patient exports, but the bulk export of all patients requires contacting MedConnectHealth\n\nNo enrichment step was needed since the documentation corpus is a single 1-page PDF with no structured data to extract."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":311,"cache_read_input_tokens":60648,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":311},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"00052a02-36e6-4e11-90d8-9e85d631cc25","uuid":"aadbbe94-0bde-4eeb-806c-5cbddd59ac25"}
